name: forgetting
description: The sense that you should have a memory of something but cannot come up with it.
results: Maybe something will jog your memory, or maybe not.
examples: Not remembering a family member's birth date.
Not remembering the code for getting into the building.

guidance.description: Tips for trying to forget something.

variations.name: uncertain memory
variations.description: Not having full confidence in your memory of something.
perceptions: I'm not confident that my memory of this fact or event is accurate.
examples: Sorry, not sure I closed the garage door.
I might remember the door code.

variations.name: just remembered
variations.description: Recalling from memory something after having forgotten it for a time.
perceptions: I had trouble getting this thing from memory.
But now that I remembered it, I'm pretty confident about it.
examples: Ok, now I remember that I for sure, closed the garage door.
I think I remember the door code now.

variations.name: someone else forgot
variations.description: A perception that someone else should have done something important by now, but has not made any effort towards doing so, nor explained why.
perceptions: That person was supposed to do this task.
And they haven't mentioned a delay.
examples: He never sent a birthday card.
He didn't pick up the bread while at the store.

commentaries.quote: Most things we remember have supporting memories as well. For example, you need to remember that you have a shopping list before remembering to get milk. If you don't remember a specific thing or any of its supporting memories, you won't experience it anymore.
The richness of life lies in memories we have forgotten.
If you want to forget something or someone, never hate it, or never hate him/her. Everything and everyone that you hate is engraved upon your heart.
The advantage of a bad memory is that one enjoys several times the same good things for the first time.
